meta.title: Synthetic Minds — AI Simulation for Complex Decisions
meta.description: Synthetic Minds is an AI simulation platform for exploring human behavior, markets, audiences, and complex scenarios before making important decisions.

home.headline: Simulate decisions before you make them.
home.supporting: Synthetic Minds creates intelligent simulated populations and environments to explore how people, markets, and complex systems may respond to change.

problem.title: Important decisions are made before the outcome is known.
problem.lead: Teams rely on surveys, historical analytics, assumptions, and stated preferences to guide major strategic decisions. But people, markets, and complex systems change when conditions change. Stated opinions reflect artificial questionnaire settings, and historical analytics only capture what happened under conditions that no longer exist.
problem.simulationLayer: Synthetic Minds adds another layer: behavioral simulation.
problem.subtext: Instead of relying only on stated preferences or past trends, explore how modeled populations respond when conditions, prices, messages, or environments change.

coreIdea.title: Ask the world a question. Simulate the response.
coreIdea.copy: Instead of relying only on stated opinions, teams can create simulated populations, introduce new conditions, and explore behavioral responses before committing to the real world.

howItWorks.title: How Synthetic Minds Works
howItWorks.subtitle: Four disciplined steps from initial definition to actionable behavioral exploration.
howItWorks.step01Desc: Create the population, environment, and context around a decision.
howItWorks.step02Desc: Test a product, price, message, strategy, policy, or scenario.
howItWorks.step03Desc: Allow simulated agents to interact under defined conditions.
howItWorks.step04Desc: Analyze behavior, patterns, responses, and possible scenarios.

explore.title: What can you explore?
explore.subtitle: Explore complex scenarios across strategic areas before committing resources.
explore.card1Desc: Explore how different audiences may respond to products, features, pricing, and positioning.
explore.card2Desc: Test messages, campaigns, offers, and creative directions across modeled audiences.
explore.card3Desc: Explore competitive moves, changing conditions, adoption scenarios, and market dynamics.
explore.card4Desc: Understand how different segments may respond under different circumstances.
explore.card5Desc: Stress-test strategic decisions across multiple possible scenarios.
explore.card6Desc: Explore how modeled populations may respond to proposed interventions and changing conditions.

populations.title: A population you can explore from every angle.
populations.copy: Build modeled populations with characteristics, goals, relationships, context, and behavioral assumptions relevant to the question you're investigating.
populations.note: Important: Synthetic agents are computational models, not real people. They provide an analytical framework for exploring possibilities under defined assumptions.

evidence.title: Ground simulations in evidence.
evidence.copy: Synthetic Minds can combine structured information, research, behavioral signals, public information, customer-provided data, and scenario assumptions to construct the context in which simulations run.
evidence.disclaimer: Simulation quality depends on the quality, relevance, and completeness of the underlying inputs and assumptions.

questions.title: What would you test if you could run the decision first?
questions.subtitle: Select a question to inspect the simulation dynamics or load it directly into the Studio.
questions.q1: Which product concept could resonate most with a target audience?
questions.a1: Simulate adoption friction, feature value perception, and willingness-to-pay across distinct demographic cohorts.
questions.q2: How might customers respond to a pricing change?
questions.a2: Observe substitution effects, churn risks, and price elasticity across sensitive customer clusters.
questions.q3: What happens if a competitor changes strategy?
questions.a3: Model rival pricing shifts, feature launches, or aggressive positioning to evaluate defense resilience.
questions.a4: Disaggregate macro sentiment to detect underlying behavioral polarization across modeled archetypes.
questions.q5: How could demand change under different market conditions?
questions.a5: Vary economic indicators, platform algorithms, or social sentiment to observe macro demand sensitivity.
questions.q6: Which strategy remains resilient across multiple scenarios?
questions.a6: Subject strategic roadmaps to adverse shocks and determine which choices withstand changing parameters.

corePositioning.headline: Ask the world a question. Simulate the response.
corePositioning.copy: Instead of relying only on stated opinions, teams can create simulated populations, introduce new conditions, and explore behavioral responses before committing to the real world.

differentiation.headline: Don't just ask what people think. Explore what they might do.
differentiation.subtitle: A fundamental shift from static feedback to dynamic agent simulation.
differentiation.card1Desc: Measures what people say they will do in an artificial questionnaire setting, often diverging from real-world behavior.
differentiation.card2Desc: Measures what happened under previous conditions that may no longer hold when prices, narratives, or competitors shift.
differentiation.card3Desc: Constructs dynamic agent populations that interact, evaluate choices, and adapt when new variables and interventions are introduced.
differentiation.disclaimer: Scientific Grounding: Simulations are rigorous instruments for exploring behavioral possibilities, mapping vulnerabilities, and challenging assumptions—not a claim of absolute prediction.

step1.ontologyDesc: LLM analyzes scenario context and simulation requirements to auto-generate a domain ontology structure
step1.graphRagDesc: Based on the generated ontology, documents are auto-chunked and sent to Zep to build a knowledge graph, extracting entities and relations, forming temporal memory and community summaries
step1.buildCompleteDesc: Graph build is complete. Proceed to the next step for simulation environment setup.

step2.simInstanceDesc: Create a new simulation instance and pull world parameter templates
step2.generateAgentPersonaDesc: Extract entities and relations from the knowledge graph, initialize simulated personas, and assign unique behaviors and memories based on scenario context
step2.dualPlatformConfigDesc: LLM intelligently sets temporal parameters, algorithmic dynamics, persona schedules, interaction frequency, and event triggers based on scenario requirements
step2.initialActivationDesc: Auto-generate initial activation events and hot topics based on narrative direction to guide the simulation world's initial state
step2.setupCompleteDesc: Simulation environment is ready. You can now start the simulation.
step2.roundsConfigDesc: Synthetic Minds auto-plans to simulate {hours} real-world hours, each round representing {minutesPerRound} minutes of elapsed time
step2.customTip: For initial runs, we recommend switching to Custom Mode to calibrate rounds for faster scenario exploration
step2.personaDimExperienceDesc: Complete behavioral trajectory in this event
